issues.item: Triggers: Sexual Trauma Cues: Comments on sexual violence
issues.explanation: For a male torture survivor, sexual-trauma-specific verbal cues are possible only if sexual torture or sexual humiliation is part of the trauma, but the rest of the profile provides no corresponding sexual content in memory, appraisals, threat, or coping. As selected, this trigger appears disconnected from the trauma representation and is hard to justify clinically.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Exposed to Others: I feel that others can see what happened to me just by looking at me
issues.explanation: The appraisal that others can visibly see what happened to him implies shame/marked visible contamination or exposure. That could occur after torture, but here it is not supported by the memory items, trigger content, or other appraisals, making it feel mismatched with the rest of the profile.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Gambling: I gamble to distract myself or feel excitement
issues.explanation: Gambling as a coping strategy is not impossible, but in this profile it is poorly linked to the active formulation. The main connected pattern is triggers ↔ negative appraisals with memory-linked re-experiencing and threat-driven compliance/detachment. Gambling introduces a separate excitement-seeking coping style that is not reflected elsewhere and feels clinically disconnected rather than integrated.

vignette: Seventy-year-old Miguel, a widowed Latin American man and a skilled welder, has been struggling with the lasting effects of torture he experienced decades ago. Despite his life now being far removed from those traumatic events, the memories persistently resurface in unexpected ways, affecting various aspects of his daily routine. The trauma began when Miguel was forced into captivity during a political uprising. He remembers feeling entrapped, with no way to escape or defend himself against the relentless violence inflicted upon him by his captors. The sound of gunshots was an ever-present reminder that he could be killed at any moment. These experiences have left deep psychological scars. In the months following his release, Miguel found it difficult to reintegrate into his life as a welder. Certain aspects of his work environment triggered memories and intense feelings of entrapment. The confined spaces in which he worked often reminded him of the suffocating conditions during his captivity. Every time he heard a loud noise, such as a gunshot or even machinery sounds that resembled gunfire, he would freeze, overwhelmed by a sense of dread. Miguel had come to believe that he could never truly feel safe again, and this belief was reinforced by his tendency to detach from memories when they became too overwhelming. He tried hard not to think about the trauma but found himself becoming overly compliant in situations where he felt threatened. This fawn response often manifested at work, where he would agree to tasks or conditions that made him uncomfortable, rather than risk conflict. The memory of his captivity still feels present and vivid rather than something from the past. When Miguel tries to explain what happened, he loses track of his thoughts and struggles to finish his sentences. These fragmented recollections are often followed by intense feelings of rage, as if the events were happening right now. Miguel's negative appraisals have also taken a significant toll on him. He fears that harm can come from anyone at any time, which has made social interactions difficult. He is consumed with guilt for not doing more to stop what happened, and he blames himself for the way his actions may have contributed to his capture. Over time, these thoughts and feelings began to affect Miguel's work and relationships. His compliance at work led to a lack of assertiveness in negotiations with his employer, resulting in unfavorable conditions that he felt powerless to change. The rage and detachment he experienced when triggered often left him isolated from colleagues who found it hard to understand why he would suddenly become distant or angry. Despite these challenges, Miguel has managed to maintain some semblance of normalcy by avoiding situations that trigger memories. However, the accumulation of guilt and self-blame has been increasingly difficult to bear. What frightened him most was the fear that he might never truly feel safe again and that he could never forgive himself for not stopping what happened. It was this overwhelming sense of helplessness that finally brought Miguel to seek help. He hoped that through therapy, he could find a way to process his memories without becoming overwhelmed by them. He was determined to reclaim his life and alleviate the guilt that had been weighing on him for so long. His journey toward healing would require confronting these deep-seated fears and negative beliefs, but Miguel felt ready to face this challenge head-on. In therapy sessions, Miguel expressed a strong desire to understand why he responds as he does and hoped to develop strategies to manage his triggers more effectively. He was eager to explore ways of reconnecting with the present without being haunted by the past, hoping that one day he could regain control over his life and finally find peace.
